definitions.explanation: A standard greeting used by staff in shops, restaurants, and other businesses when a customer enters. Derived from the honorific verb いらっしゃる (to be/come/go).

examples.japanese: いらっしゃいませ、{何名様|なんめいさま}ですか。
examples.english: Welcome. How many in your party?

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}に{入|はい}ると、{店員|てんいん}が{元気|げんき}よく「いらっしゃいませ」と{声|こえ}をかけてきた。
examples.english: When I entered the shop, a clerk called out a cheerful "Welcome!"

notes:
One of the most frequently heard expressions in daily life in Japan. Said by staff when a customer enters a shop, restaurant, or business.

ETYMOLOGY:
Derived from いらっしゃる, the honorific form of {来|く}る (to come) / いる (to be). The ませ ending adds polite invitation.

RESPONSE:
Customers do not need to reply. A slight nod or smile is sufficient.

FORMS:
- いらっしゃい: less formal version (small shops, welcoming someone home)
- いらっしゃいませ〜: drawn-out, sing-song style (busy shops, izakaya)

USAGE:
- In busy restaurants and shops, multiple staff may call this out in unison
- Also used when a customer approaches a counter or when acknowledged for the first time
- Not used between equals — strictly a service/hospitality greeting
